tagline: Up Looking Glass Creek to where American forestry went to school.
intro: The byway starts at a pair of stone pillars on US 276 outside Brevard, the gate to the Pisgah National Forest, where an arch once stood. It follows the Davidson River and Looking Glass Creek upstream, past Looking Glass Falls and Sliding Rock, to the Cradle of Forestry and the Pink Beds, an upland bog grown thick with rhododendron and laurel. Then it switchbacks up Pisgah Ridge, crosses the Blue Ridge Parkway at Wagon Road Gap, 4,528 feet, and comes down to Shining Creek Gap.
The woods look old and are not. More than a century ago this valley was logged and farmed, and stretches of the road run on the old logging railroad grades.

moments.title: Looking Glass Falls
moments.text: A 60-foot fall right at the side of the road, with a path down to the plunge pool. In winter it freezes solid and the ice climbers come.

moments.title: Sliding Rock
moments.text: Looking Glass Creek slides down 60 feet of gently sloping rock into an eight-foot pool that stays near 55 degrees all year. Sliding is done sitting upright.

moments.title: Cradle of Forestry
moments.text: Carl Schenck's Biltmore Forest School opened here a few weeks ahead of Cornell's in 1898, the first in North America, though Schenck said there was never a formal opening.

practical: US 276 has 9% grades and slow curves, and the byway is not recommended for recreational vehicles or buses.
